blocks.text: Isaiah 22 belongs within a wider book that addresses Judah, Israel, and foreign nations. Across Isaiah, empires can be portrayed as instruments in the story while also remaining accountable themselves; the book also includes visions of nations learning, worshiping, and sharing in restoration. This broader pattern helps place the chapter’s judgment of Judah alongside Isaiah’s wider concern with both local and international peoples.

The text of Isaiah is witnessed by the Great Isaiah Scroll, an almost complete copy of all sixty-six chapters that broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition while containing many spelling and substantive differences. Other Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings from Qumran also show that the book was actively copied and interpreted.
